gate: M4-052 P0 — document that v0.1 is not plugin sandbox

cases.requirement: The public v0.1 documentation explicitly states that DSH Safe Runtime is not a sandbox for arbitrary in-process plugins.
The non-sandbox statement is scoped to current v0.1/in-process plugin execution rather than future isolated-host designs.
Documentation distinguishes behavior that reaches ToolRuntime/tool PEP seams from arbitrary same-process host API calls.
Documentation preserves the existing rule that ToolRuntime policy is not arbitrary in-process plugin isolation.
cases.evidence: Existing README non-negotiable boundary plus Spec 0052 section 2.1.

cases.requirement: Documentation preserves the distinction between tool-enforced and process-isolated guarantees.
Documentation does not describe the current plugin execution model as process-isolated, filesystem-isolated, host-isolated, or sandboxed.
M4-050 direct-host filesystem evidence remains the authority for the accepted EXPECTED_UNGOVERNED host-API witness.
M4-052 does not relabel the M4-050 negative witness as ALLOW, DENY, SANDBOXED, or process-isolated.
M4-051 remains authority only for shell-string nested-effect matcher incompleteness while recognized shell calls remain process.exec.
The plugin-sandbox non-claim is not rewritten into the false claim that every shell call is ungoverned.
The top-level README carries a concise discoverable non-sandbox statement.
The architecture documentation provides the precise technical boundary behind the README non-claim.
M14 remains the explicit future owner of process-isolated plugin hosting.
cases.evidence: Roadmap M14 plus Spec 0052 sections 2.5 and 13.

cases.requirement: Documentation does not claim that any M14 worker, RPC, supervisor, OS backend, or security milestone is already implemented.
M4-052 makes no production runtime enforcement change.
M4-052 adds no new Capability protocol wire type, Schema vocabulary, policy effect, or GuaranteeLevel.
Documentation does not present tool-name allowlists, raw shell string matching, coding conventions, or prose promises as substitutes for process isolation.
M6 workspace transactionality is not described as equivalent to arbitrary plugin sandboxing.
M12 brokered/provider network enforcement is not prematurely described as complete same-process plugin isolation.
Future architecture intent is distinguishable from current accepted security guarantees.
Documentation does not claim that documentation changes runtime security or converts an ungoverned effect into a governed one.
M4-052 does not prematurely create or claim completion of the later M17 security review or M19 Security Model/Known Limitations program.
Harness-specific ToolRuntime claims remain pinned to rc5 source/runtime evidence and do not become process-isolation claims.
cases.evidence: Spec 0052 section 15 and pinned Harness workflow.

cases.requirement: Protocol-first, later-Gate separation, roadmap state, and PR #3 merge authorization remain governed independently of documentation wording.
